title: Finite-type points detect surjectivity of flat locally presented maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, $A$ an algebraic space over $S$, and $q:A\to\mathcal X$ a flat locally finitely presented morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with these properties tested on scheme charts. If the image of $|q|:|A|\to|\mathcal X|$ contains every finite-type point of $\mathcal X$, then $q$ is surjective: for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the algebraic space $A\times_{\mathcal X}T$ maps surjectively to $T$. The set $|\mathcal X|$ consists of field-valued objects modulo the equivalence identifying two objects when they become isomorphic over a common field extension. A point is of finite type if it has a representative $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal X$ locally of finite type. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product and representability by algebraic spaces use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts.

source.place: Tag 06G2 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points), combined with stacks-properties.tex Tags 04XL (lemma-topology-points), (2), and 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective); the open-image criterion used in the final paragraph of theorem-DM.

proof.text: Because $\mathcal X$ is algebraic, its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] to its fibred groupoid and $q:A\to\mathcal X$. Thus $q$ is representable by algebraic spaces and, for each scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the 2-fibre product $A\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is an algebraic space. This verifies the representability hypothesis needed for the final point-surjectivity criterion.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), implication (1) => (7); (8) also gives the stated fibre products.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open] to the given $q:A\to\mathcal X$. Its point classes identify field-valued objects after a common field extension, exactly the equivalence relation defining $|\mathcal X|$ in the statement; for $A$ its topology agrees with the usual algebraic-space topology. Thus its induced map is the same $|q|$ whose image occurs in the hypothesis. The given chartwise flatness and local finite presentation meet the openness assertion, so $|q|$ is open. Since the whole $|A|$ is open in itself, $O=|q|(|A|)$ is open in $|\mathcal X|$.

source.place: Tags 04XG (definition-points) and 04XL (lemma-topology-points), parts (1), (2), and the smooth-atlas description in its proof.

proof.text: The complement $Z=|\mathcal X|\setminus O$ is closed and hence locally closed, being its own intersection with the whole open space. Suppose $Z$ were nonempty. By [lem-sfb-stack-locally-closed-finite-type-point], it would contain a point $x$ represented by a locally finite-type map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$. This is exactly the finite-type-point convention in the hypothesis, so $x\in O$, contradicting $x\in Z$. Therefore $Z=\varnothing$, so $O=|\mathcal X|$ and $|q|$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 06G2 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points), applied to the closed complement, as in the final paragraph of Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-representable-stack-point-surjectivity] to $f=q$, whose source $\mathcal Y=A$ is an algebraic space, a case that lemma allows, with representability from step 1 and surjectivity of $|q|$ from step 3. Its conclusion gives, for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, surjectivity on points of $A\times_{\mathcal X}T\to T$. This is exactly the asserted surjectivity of $q$; finite-type-point detection is used on $\mathcal X$ itself, so no assertion about preserving finite-type points under an arbitrary $T\to\mathcal X$ is needed.

lean.statement: theorem stack_flat_lfp_finite_type_surjectivity {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (A : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli A.obj.obj) F) (hflat : ModuliSpaceTest @Flat q) (hlfp : ModuliSpaceTest @LocallyOfFinitePresentation q) (hfinite : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk s))) F), ModuliSpaceTest @LocallyOfFiniteType a → Set.range (moduliPointMap a) ⊆ Set.range (moduliPointMap q)) : ∀ (T : Over S) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) F), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange q T t Z p ∧ SpaceMapIsSurjective Z T p
lean.note: The finite-type-point image hypothesis is quantified directly over all locally finite-type maps from field spectra. Uses the existing field-object quotient, actual point maps, chartwise property tests, and projection-compatible algebraic-space base-change presentations; no replacement point notion or stronger stack hypothesis.
